articles.nri_angle: India's ability to maintain working relationships with both Washington and Tehran through the BRICS presidency directly determines the safety of nine million Indians in the Gulf, the stability of energy prices affecting diaspora families, and the remittance corridors that fund communities back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One Indian Crew Member Is Missing After Iran Attacked a Container Ship in the Strait of Hormuz. India Has Condemned the Strike.
articles.excerpt: The GFS Galaxy was carrying 11 Indian nationals when Iran's IRGC Navy struck it Saturday, calling it a warning shot at an 'unauthorised' vessel. Ten Indians were rescued. The search for one continues.
articles.image_caption: NASA MODIS satellite image of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman where the GFS Galaxy was attacked
articles.nri_angle: Indian seafarers face disproportionate risk as Iran-US war destabilises the Strait of Hormuz — one Indian crew member is missing and over 6,000 are stranded across the Gulf.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The European Parliament Just Condemned Pakistan for the Forced Conversion of Hindu and Christian Girls. The Numbers Are Staggering.
articles.excerpt: Seventy-five per cent of forced conversion victims in Pakistan are Hindu. The EU resolution calls out a court ruling that validated the marriage of a 13-year-old Christian girl to her 30-year-old abductor.
articles.image_caption: The European Parliament hemicycle in Strasbourg, France, where members voted on the resolution condemning forced conversions in Pakistan
articles.nri_angle: Seventy-five per cent of Pakistan's forced conversion victims are Hindu — the EU resolution reinforces concerns held by the Indian diaspora and backs India's long-standing push for minority rights protection in Pakistan.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Lindsey Graham, the Senate's Loudest Voice on Iran and India, Dies at 71. His Empty Chair Changes the Calculus for Both.
articles.excerpt: The South Carolina senator — Budget Committee chairman, immigration deal-maker, and the man who pressed Trump hardest on the Iran war now shaping life for nine million Indians in the Gulf — died of cardiac arrest Saturday night, a day after meeting Zelensky in Kyiv.
articles.image_caption: Senator Lindsey Graham in his official 113th Congress portrait
articles.nri_angle: Graham shaped key immigration policy including H-1B visa reform debates, championed the US-India defense partnership, and drove the Iran war policy now directly affecting nine million Indians in the Gulf — his absence shifts Senate dynamics on all three fronts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian Immigrant's Son Launches to the Space Station on Monday. He Spent a Year in India Vaccinating Children Against Polio.
articles.excerpt: NASA astronaut Anil Menon — born to a Kerala-origin father and a Ukrainian mother in Minneapolis — lifts off aboard Soyuz MS-29 on July 14 for an eight-month mission. He is a Harvard neuroscientist, Stanford physician, former SpaceX flight surgeon, and the latest in a growing line of Indian-origin Americans reaching orbit.
articles.image_caption: NASA astronaut Anil Menon in his official portrait at Johnson Space Center
articles.nri_angle: Menon is the son of an Indian immigrant from Kerala and spent a formative year in India on a Rotary scholarship fighting polio — his launch is one of the most visible achievements by an Indian-American in the US space programme, following Kalpana Chawla, Sunita Williams, and Raja Chari.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Iran War Just Went Gulf-Wide. For Nine Million Indians in the Region, the Fight Is Now Overhead.
articles.excerpt: Iranian missiles struck targets in five Gulf states in a single day. The U.S. hit 300 targets in three nights. The Strait of Hormuz is closed again. And India's largest overseas community is caught in the middle.
articles.image_caption: A U.S. Navy supply vessel transits the Strait of Hormuz, the strategic waterway through which one-fifth of the world's oil supply passes
articles.nri_angle: Nine million Indians in the Gulf — the largest expatriate community in the region — are directly affected as Iranian strikes expand to five countries where they live and work, while 6,000 Indian seafarers remain stranded and Gulf remittances worth $28 billion face disruption.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Biggest Trade Deal Goes Live on Tuesday. Here's What Changes for the Diaspora in Britain.
articles.excerpt: The India-UK free trade agreement enters force on July 15, cutting tariffs to near zero on 99 per cent of Indian exports, eliminating dual social security payments for 75,000 professionals, and creating mobility pathways for IT workers, chefs and musicians.
articles.image_caption: India's Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal, who led the trade agreement negotiations
articles.nri_angle: The 1.9 million Indians in Britain are directly affected: 75,000 professionals will stop paying double social security, 99% of Indian exports get duty-free access making Indian goods cheaper in UK shops, and 1,800 chefs, yoga instructors and musicians get dedicated work visas annually.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Supreme Court Just Saved Birthright Citizenship. For Half a Million Indian Families on Temporary Visas, It Was Never Abstract.
articles.excerpt: A 6-3 ruling strikes down Trump's executive order denying automatic citizenship to children born to H-1B, H-4, and other temporary visa holders — preserving a right that quietly underpins Indian America.
articles.image_caption: The United States Supreme Court building in Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: Over 5.4 million Indian Americans, most on temporary visas with decades-long green card waits, would have seen their U.S.-born children denied citizenship had the order stood.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Just Closed the Strait of Hormuz 'Until Further Notice.' India Has Spent Four Months Preparing for Exactly This.
articles.excerpt: A struck vessel, a formal closure, and a collapsing ceasefire — but India's petroleum minister says the country's crisis playbook has kept pumps open and prices lower than anywhere in the world.
articles.image_caption: Satellite or aerial view of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway through which a fifth of the world's oil once flowed
articles.nri_angle: Six thousand Indian seafarers remain trapped in the Gulf, and the closure threatens India's fragile energy recovery — raising inflation, weakening the rupee, and straining supply lines that NRI remittances help sustain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Six Thousand Seafarers Are Trapped in the Gulf. For Indian Sailors, the War Has Become Personal.
articles.excerpt: Three Indian crew members are dead. One sailor watched 140 missiles fly in 30 minutes. Thousands more are stranded on ships running low on food and fuel. India is sending diplomats. The sailors want a way home.
articles.image_caption: Satellite image of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman where thousands of ships and seafarers remain stranded
articles.nri_angle: Roughly 23,000 Indians work on merchant and offshore vessels in the Gulf region — India is one of the world's top three suppliers of seafarers, and the Iran war has killed three Indian crew members while trapping thousands more on ships under fire.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Sold Its Most Powerful Missile to a Third Country. The $630 Million Deal Rewrites the Indo-Pacific Arms Map.
articles.excerpt: Indonesia becomes the third nation to buy the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile, after the Philippines and Vietnam. India's defence exports have grown thirty-five-fold in a decade.
articles.image_caption: BrahMos supersonic cruise missile system on display during India's Republic Day parade in New Delhi
articles.nri_angle: India's transformation from the world's largest arms importer to a meaningful defence exporter — with combat-proven systems now deployed across Southeast Asia — marks a generational shift in the country's global standing that NRIs have long advocated for.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Signs a Strategic Partnership in Auckland. Outside the Arena, 300,000 Indian Kiwis Are Living Through a Racism Crisis.
articles.excerpt: India and New Zealand elevated ties to a strategic partnership on Saturday — the first such visit by an Indian PM in 40 years — but the trade deal that brought Modi to Auckland has also unleashed a 'butter chicken tsunami' of anti-Indian backlash.
articles.image_caption: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his three-nation Asia-Pacific tour
articles.nri_angle: Modi's historic visit to New Zealand comes amid a surge in anti-Indian racism that has made the 292,000-strong Indian community a flashpoint in the country's immigration debate — a pattern disturbingly familiar to diaspora communities worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian American Congressman Was Detained at Gunpoint in the West Bank. He Says It Made Him More Likely to Run for President.
articles.excerpt: Ro Khanna says armed Israeli settlers surrounded his van with M4 rifles, held his group for over an hour, and the IDF sided with the settlers — an experience he says strengthened his resolve to seek the White House in 2028.
articles.image_caption: Ro Khanna, Democratic congressman from California, at a congressional hearing
articles.nri_angle: Ro Khanna, one of the most prominent Indian American lawmakers in Congress, was detained by armed Israeli settlers while visiting the West Bank — an incident that has intensified his consideration of a 2028 presidential run and raised questions about Indian American political identity.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian-American CEO Laid Off 1,600 Xbox Workers. Days Later, the Fed Appointed Her to an Advisory Panel. The Internet Did the Rest.
articles.excerpt: Asha Sharma was born in Wisconsin, ran Instacart through its IPO, and was personally chosen by Satya Nadella to lead Xbox. None of that stopped critics from reducing her to her ethnicity.
articles.image_caption: Asha Sharma at the 2026 Xbox Showcase, shortly after being named CEO of Microsoft Gaming
articles.nri_angle: An American-born Indian-origin tech executive faces explicitly racial backlash over corporate layoffs, exposing how the H-1B debate can become a vehicle for targeting Indian Americans in leadership.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Rules, One Target: The Trump Administration Is Rewriting Every Immigration Pathway Indians Use to Live in America
articles.excerpt: H-1B placements face new scrutiny, Green Card wage floors are doubling, student visas will expire, and 100,000 H-4 spouses could lose work authorization — all by August.
articles.image_caption: The United States Capitol at dusk in Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: The proposed rules collectively target every major immigration pathway used by Indian professionals, students, and families — H-1B, H-4, OPT, F-1, and Green Cards — with changes that could take effect within weeks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Tells Washington Its Forced Labour Tariff Case Has No Evidence. The Hearing Got Personal.
articles.excerpt: At the USTR's Section 301 hearings, India's government and industry groups dismantled the case for a 12.5 per cent duty — while a ticking clock on July 24 makes the fight existential.
articles.image_caption: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer has overseen the Section 301 investigation
articles.nri_angle: A 12.5% tariff on Indian goods would raise costs for Indian American consumers, squeeze IT services supply chains, and threaten the mid-sized exporters that connect India's economy to the US market.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Inflation Just Breached the Central Bank's Red Line. The Iran War and a Weak Monsoon Are Making It Worse.
articles.excerpt: Consumer prices are expected to have topped the RBI's 4 per cent target in June for the first time in sixteen months, with food, fuel and El Niño piling on pressure.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India tower in Mumbai, headquarters of the central bank that sets monetary policy
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with Indian equity, bond and real estate exposure face eroding real returns and a tighter RBI, while remittance values shift with the rupee's trajectory.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NYC's Indian-Origin Mayor Is Under Fire for an Immigrant Map That Erased Little Italy, Irish, and Jewish New York
articles.excerpt: Zohran Mamdani's well-intentioned immigrant heritage project sparked outrage by omitting iconic European-immigrant neighborhoods — exposing how even progressive diversity efforts can erase history.
articles.image_caption: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who took office in January 2026, has faced his first major cultural controversy over the city's interactive immigrant heritage map.
articles.nri_angle: Mamdani, born in Uganda to a family of Indian and Ugandan descent, is NYC's first mayor of South Asian heritage. The controversy highlights how immigrant identity politics in America's most diverse city directly affect how diaspora communities — including Indian Americans — see their history represented in public institutions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Federal Judge Just Killed Trump's $100,000 H-1B Fee. The Rest of the Crackdown Is Just Getting Started.
articles.excerpt: The ruling is a win for tech companies and Indian workers — but a wave of site visits, RFEs, and revocations means the H-1B system is still under siege.
articles.image_caption: A USCIS Application Support Center in Queens, New York. The agency has dramatically escalated H-1B enforcement actions in 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals receive approximately 72-75% of all H-1B visas annually. Every policy change to the H-1B system disproportionately affects the Indian diaspora — from tech workers in Silicon Valley to families waiting decades in the green card backlog. The fee ruling and ongoing enforcement wave are reshaping the landscape for hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals in America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Goes Directly to Iran to Secure Passage for Nine Trapped Tankers and 198 Stranded Sailors
articles.excerpt: With three Indian seafarers dead and an Indian supertanker forced to U-turn at Hormuz, the Modi government is opening its own diplomatic channel to Tehran — sidestepping a stalled American peace deal.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker docked at the Al Basrah Oil Terminal takes on crude in the Persian Gulf
articles.nri_angle: Indian seafarers are dying in Gulf crossfire, oil prices threaten NRI household budgets worldwide, and India's LPG lifeline runs through the same choked strait.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian Immigrant's Son Just Entered One of America's Most Consequential Senate Races
articles.excerpt: Dr Nirav Shah, who led Maine through COVID-19 and served as the CDC's second-in-command, is now running for Susan Collins's Senate seat. If he wins the nomination, he would be the first South Asian to run for Senate from New England.
articles.image_caption: The Maine State House in Augusta, where Democrats are scrambling to name a Senate nominee
articles.nri_angle: An Indian American — son of immigrants from India and former CDC deputy director — is now a leading candidate for the U.S. Senate in Maine, a test of South Asian political power at the highest level.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Just Gutted the Only Federal Agency Devoted to Election Security. Four Months Before the Midterms.
articles.excerpt: The president fired the last two members of the Election Assistance Commission on Thursday, leaving the body unable to certify voting systems, distribute security funds, or maintain the national voter registration form — as the administration simultaneously pushes states to purge voter rolls of naturalized citizens.
articles.image_caption: The U.S. Election Assistance Commission, now without any commissioners for the first time in its history
articles.nri_angle: The gutting of the EAC comes alongside voter-roll purge systems that disproportionately flag naturalized citizens — including the 2.7 million Indian Americans who are U.S. citizens — as ineligible to vote.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
